title: Terraform IAM policy skeleton + enforcement hooks for private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Delivery of a lightweight Terraform module that scaffolds IAM/RBAC resources and provides opinionated enforcement hooks (policy attachments, validation checks, helper outputs) for Private/VPC deployments. Module goal: enable SREs and infra engineers to bootstrap least-privilege roles/policies and to integrate runtime enforcement (pre-apply checks, CI gating) without manual RBAC policy churn.
acceptance_criteria: Module lives under infra/terraform/modules/priv_iam and follows Redwood naming conventions
Module exposes variables for tenant/resource names, environment, and allowed service principals
Produces IAM role templates, policy documents, and binding resources (no hard-coded ARNs)
Includes Terraform `pre-apply` validation script and a `policy_lint` command for CI
Automated upgrade path documented (v1 -> v2): migration script and audit log of changes
Unit tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform) validate policy least-priv and deny-over-permissive rules
Security review checklist completed and review comments addressed
tasks: Draft module API (inputs/outputs) and examples for customer and internal cloud
Implement policy template generator for JSON policy documents
Add pre-apply validation hook (tf validate + custom lint)
Create CI workflow to run policy_lint on PRs
Write example overlay for Dedicated vs Private footprints
Add migration script for policy renames and role ARN changes
Write terratest suite covering 3 resource shapes (small/generic/enterprise)
Create docs page in Confluence and link examples
design_decisions: Use data-driven policy templates instead of multiple hard-coded modules to reduce duplication
Expose coarse-grained grants; require consumers to opt-into broader permissions via explicit variables
Default to deny-list approach for newly created roles; allow overrides via `allow_list` variable
Keep audit log of generated policies in S3 bucket for upgrade diffing
Don't attempt to manage account-wide service control policies (out of scope) — focus on resource-level role/policy bindings
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal infra teams only — feature-flag deployment and `--dry-run` pre-apply checks
Beta: enable for 2 pilot customers with SRE support, monitor workload routing
GA: publish module in Terraform registry, mark as supported with upgrade playbook and runbook
Fallback: rollback to previous policy artifacts stored in repo and S3 versioned bucket
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + custom lint rules locally
Integration: terratest create/destroy in a disposable AWS account
Upgrade test: run migration script between v1->v2 in a sandbox and assert no permission gaps
CI: PRs must pass policy_lint and terratest smoke suite before merge
E2E: create test tenant in staging and exercise typical Redwood API flows to detect permission errors
notes: Aligns with runtime assumptions in runtime-1.18 about service principals; coordinate with ENG-170221 for templated role naming
KMS/HSM key bindings will be referenced but not managed by this module — coordinate with security for KMS IAM patterns
Consider embedding a JSON schema for generated policy documents to simplify linting
Will iterate on curations after pilot feedback to reduce false positives from lint
